'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[2021 evacuation from Afghanistan]]
***[[Operation Pitting]]
****Former [[Royal Military Police]] soldier Ben Slater is briefly arrested for questioning by the [[Taliban]] while trying to evacuate 400 Afghans and 50 staff members. [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/south-asia/british-soldier-mission-taliban-arrest-b1913200.html (''The Independent'')]
**Aftermath of the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]], [[Capital punishment in Afghanistan]], [[LGBT rights in Afghanistan]]
***Afghan [[LGBT rights in Afghanistan|LGBT rights]] activist [[Nemat Sadat]] and an unnamed gay man in [[Kabul]] both report that the Taliban beheaded the man's boyfriend on the same day that they entered the city. Sadat said that while women are only executed if they commit [[adultery]], homosexuals face an "automatic [[death sentence]] based on their mere existence". [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-02/afghans-lgbt-community-face-stoning-under-taliban-law/100412330 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[Panjshir conflict]]
***The Taliban enters the [[Panjshir Valley]] and clashes with [[National Resistance Front of Afghanistan]] forces led by [[Ahmad Massoud]]. The Taliban reports gaining some territory as both sides also claim heavy casualties. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-afghan-rebels-claim-heavy-casualties-fighting-over-valley-2021-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli soldiers]] open fire on [[Palestinians]] protesting against Israel's 14-year blockade of the [[Gaza Strip]], killing one person and injuring 15 others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/2/israeli-troops-shoot-dead-palestinian-during-gaza-demonstrations (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**[[Indian government|Indian authorities]] deploy [[Indian Armed Forces|security forces]] in the [[Kashmir Valley]] in order to restrict public movement and impose a near-total [[internet blackout]] following the death of senior [[Kashmiri separatist|separatist leader]] [[Syed Ali Shah Geelani]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210901-security-clampdown-in-indian-kashmir-after-death-of-separatist-icon-geelani (France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Hurricane Ida]]
**At least 41 people are killed by [[flash flood|flash flooding]] and [[tornado|tornados]] in [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Pennsylvania]], [[Maryland]], [[Virginia]], and [[New Jersey]] as the remnants of Ida pass over the [[Northeastern United States]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-us-canada-58420997 (BBC News)]
*Twelve people are dead and 4,500 are sick in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] following a toxic leak from a massive [[diamond mine]] in [[Angola]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58432578 (BBC News)]
* A plane crashes into a building killing all 4 onboard and injured two on the ground in [[Farmington]], [[United States]]. [https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/plane-crashes-into-building-in-farmington-police/2574190/ (CT)]
* A minibus overturned and plunged off a road into a valley in [[Kurdish province]], [[Iran]] killing 16 and injuring 12.[https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/mini-bus-plunges-off-road-into-a-valley-in-iran-killing-16/articleshow/85864273.cms (THE TIMES OF INDIA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 3,805 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 221,351. [https://m.akipress.com/news:662085:Mongolia_reported_a_record_of_3,805_new_COVID-19_cases/ (AKI Press)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports 191 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, including 187 locally transmitted cases. It is the highest number of locally-transmitted cases since August 7, 2020. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/covid-19-new-cases-sep-2-local-unlinked-bus-interchange-clusters-2151011 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] receives its first shipment of 932,000 doses of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.asahi.com/sp/ajw/articles/14431805 (''The Asahi Shimbun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Emirate of Abu Dhabi|Abu Dhabi]] will lift its [[quarantine]] requirements for all vaccinated foreign travellers on September 5 as long as they show a negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 testing|test]] result as the [[UAE]] reported no COVID-19 deaths in the past 24 hours for the first time since November 14, 2020. [https://www.barrons.com/news/abu-dhabi-eases-tourist-quarantines-as-uae-hits-zero-deaths-01630593307 (''Barron's'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****[[Philippe of Belgium|King Philippe]] and [[Queen Mathilde of Belgium|Queen Mathilde]] cancel or reschedule their attendance at all public events and engagements, in addition to placing all [[Monarchy of Belgium|members of the Royal Family]] into [[quarantine]], after a Royal Family member [[COVID-19 testing|tested positive]] for COVID-19. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-member-of-belgian-royal-family-tests-positive-for-covid-19/ (''The Globe and Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****The [[Bulgaria]]n [[Government of Bulgaria|government]] announces nationwide restrictions that would require restaurants, bars, and casinos to close at 10 p.m., restrict the capacity of gyms, theatres, and cinemas to between 30% to 50%, and ban all mass gatherings from September 7 until October 30 amid the spread of COVID-19 and the low percentage of [[COVID-19 vaccination in Bulgaria|vaccinated]] people. [https://seenews.com/news/bulgaria-to-tighten-covid-19-restrictions-as-of-sept-7-752815 (See News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Norway]]
****[[Prime Minister of Norway|Prime Minister]] [[Erna Solberg]] announces that children aged 12 to 15 years old in [[Norway]] will be offered the single-dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. However, only the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] that is currently recommended for this age group. [https://www.fhi.no/en/news/2021/12-15-year-olds-will-be-offered-coronavirus-vaccination/ (Norwegian Institute of Public Health)] 
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]]
***[[Kenya]] receives a shipment of 358,200 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] donated by [[Canada]] as part of the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/kenya-receives-nearly-360-000-doses-of-coronavirus-vaccine-from-canada/2353611 (Anadolu Agency)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**[[Poland]] declares a [[state of emergency]] on its [[Belarus–Poland border|border]] with [[Belarus]] amid an increase in [[Illegal immigration|illegal migration]]. The [[Border Guard (Poland)|Polish Border Guard]] says that there were around 3,500 attempts to illegally cross the border in August, 2,500 of which were not successful. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-president-imposes-state-emergency-belarus-border-2021-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Afghanistan–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[British Foreign Secretary]] [[Dominic Raab]] announces that there is no "foreseeable recognition" of the [[Taliban government]] in [[Afghanistan]] although he asserts that the [[United Kingdom]] will nevertheless directly engage the group in necessary talks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/2/taliban-shows-us-plunder-as-kabul-flight-resumes-after-withdrawal (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Aftermath of the [[Dar es Salaam shooting]]
**Authorities in [[Tanzania]] have confirmed that the gunman who killed three policemen and a security guard in [[Dar es Salaam]] on August 25, was motivated by [[Islamic extremism]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tanzania-says-gunman-who-killed-four-people-last-month-was-terrorist-2021-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
**[[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] signs a law allowing vaccine and medication patents to be broken in situations of public health emergency in [[Brazil]], such as the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazils-bolsonaro-signs-law-that-could-break-covid-19-vaccine-patents-2021-09-02/ (Reuters)]
